R1.reason: p2 contribution bullet expressly constructs DF3; §IV pp6–7 documents reusable systematic resource; §V.D p8 describes Mixed subset as a tool for future detector robustness; conclusion p11 names planned code/dataset-details release.

scientific_review.empirical_validity: Counts and performance are manuscript-reported; synthetic variants share base images and should not be treated as independent samples. No independent performance replication.
scientific_review.causal_interpretation: Post-processing suppression of high-frequency traces and real-world representativeness are hypotheses/interpretations, not causal conclusions validated by this review.
scientific_review.availability: p11 promises code and dataset details will be released at github.com/littlejuyan/GLFF. This is future-tense, not proof that dataset/code were available at capture or that images/license are downloadable.
scientific_review.reproducibility: Detailed construction parameters and counts support contribution classification; no code, dataset, manifests or seeds were executed/verified. Dataset excludes real controls; p8 separately selects 1,000 FFHQ negatives for metric calculation.

evidence.locator: Contribution list p2; §IV DF3 Dataset p6; Table I p6
evidence.claim: DF3 constructs fake faces from StyleGAN2, StyleGAN3, 3DGAN, Transformers, LSGM and Latent-diffusion, followed by five post-processing families. Six tabulated protocols include unprocessed originals as protocol 1.

Common processing uses JPEG quality randomly selected in [20,90], Gaussian blur sigma in [1,4] or both; face blending uses SimSwap with FFHQ-unaligned and manual removal of failed outputs. Anti-forensics randomly uses CW or GANPrintR; multi-image compression groups still images as an H.264 sequence in HandBrake at quality 22 then extracts images. Mixed combines two/three processing families.

evidence.locator: §V.C/D p8; Table II p8; Conclusion p11
evidence.claim: DF3 is fake-only; 1,000 separately sampled FFHQ real controls enable AUC. Resource is intended for future robustness evaluation, with planned code/dataset-details release. Face blending introduces manipulated-face content; H.264 is an image post-processing construction step, not evidence of a video-detection task.

quantitative_evidence.locator: Table I p6; Table II p8
quantitative_evidence.caveat: Narrative says approximately 46,400; exact table total is 46,476. Total includes related processed derivatives of 6,160 base images, not 46,476 independent generated images.
Around 1,000 per model is approximate; preserve unequal source counts.

quantitative_evidence.reported: Five post-processing families plus unprocessed = six evaluation protocols. Five baseline detectors; Nodown uses released pretrained weights, others retrained. AUCs average across six models, then protocols.
quantitative_evidence.caveat: CW attacks CNN-aug; paper excludes CNN-aug from anti-forensics comparison for fairness. Table averages/negative-class reuse and tailored attacks limit universal superiority interpretations.

limitations: Face-only resource includes generated faces blended/swapped into real scenes; preserve this as a separate manipulation category description without changing current tasks or image scopes.
Author version only; publisher-final content and bibliographic linkage not independently compared.
Future-tense code/dataset-details release is weaker than verified current dataset availability; no license or files fetched.
No R2 benchmark label proposed; no attribution or video task inferred.
confidence: High for R1 contribution support in identified arXiv v7; moderate for publisher-version bridge and operational availability.
